messages:
maya: Quick thread  autofallback exceptions + SLA implications. If a policy triggers fallback for X% of traffic, do we treat that as an SLO breach or as expected behavior? Need default wording for hosted + Dedicated. @chen @owen

chen: If a configured fallback policy exists, it shouldn't count as a breach unless the fallback changes expected contract (e.g., schema change) or breaches latency SLOs. We need explicit mapping: fallback->severity mapping.

owen: agree. default: fallback events are informational. escalate to warn if >5% of requests in 5m or if errors increase. that keeps noise down.

priya: UX/console: show a clear banner when a policy is active for a tenant with counts and a projected SLO risk. also add a checkbox in rollout to opt into counting fallbacks as failures for strict customers.

maya: good. telemetry: include fields: fallback_id, policy_id, rate_pct, trigger, samples_link (signed). sampling default 0.1%.

sam-bot: note: created ticket RW-14077 "Fallback severity mapping + SLA language" assigned to maya, chen, owen, priya.

chen: also need billing note: if fallback reduces billed tokens, record both billed_estimate and logical_estimate in events so customers can reconcile.

owen: implementation plan: 1) severity mapping config; 2) header + audit events; 3) console banner + opt-in toggle; 4) docs + SLA wording. owners: maya->RFC, chen->telemetry + billing, priy a->console UX. quick reactions?

priya: +1

chen: +1

owen: +1
